clue.text: An argument for change

definitions.meaning: an alteration, as in 'it makes all the ...'

explanation.surface: Someone puts forward a case in favour of change.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a disagreement between people and the alteration that sets one thing apart from another.

clue.text: Sarcastic order is about right

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture

explanation.surface: A remark that the command is about right is meant scornfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command but is an architectural order (Doric, Ionic, Corinthian); 'about' puts R inside IONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarcastic remark says the opposite of what is meant, which is the essence of irony.

clue.text: In the buff, tribe start the dance

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or fan
Dan is one of the twelve tribes of Israel
to go is to start, as in 'ready, steady, go'

explanation.surface: Naked tribesmen begin a ritual dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the buff' looks like nakedness, but 'buff' alone is an enthusiast; 'In the' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish dance for couples.

clue.text: Complaint of one summer hat being ruined

indicators.note: a hat that is ruined is wrecked, so its letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that their summer hat has been spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being ruined' rearranges I (one) with SUMMER and HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment, and rheumatism is a painful one of the joints.

clue.text: Making, a home? Someone's tinged with envy!

indicators.note: with here means the words carry the letters within them, held inside their run

explanation.surface: Someone envious is going green while setting up house.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'someONE'S TINGed'; 'envy' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds building their nest are making a home, and the word is now used of people setting up house.

clue.text: Made up in the Netherlands

definitions.note: a place phrase standing for a town found there

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word Made is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Something was fabricated in Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' looks like 'invented', but in a down clue 'up' turns MADE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a town in the Netherlands, famous for its round cheese.

clue.text: Computer control for a girl's credit

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name, and the 's adds an S
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A computer device is credited to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is a lever used to steer the action in computer games.

clue.text: Man to entertain with style at the Palace

parts.note: Ken is a man's name
to sing is to entertain an audience
ton is fashion or style, as in 'bon ton'

explanation.surface: A man performs stylishly at a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington Palace is a royal residence in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Kensington Palace is a royal residence in London, so the name stands for that palace.

clue.text: Get the message to fish in the river

indicators.note: in places the fish within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, Wales and England, a crossword favourite
the cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go fishing in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the message' looks like an instruction, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a coded message is to work out what it says.

clue.text: Moves against bars

definitions.meaning: to counter is to act in opposition
the long tops in shops or pubs over which goods or drinks are served

explanation.surface: A pub-goer acts against the bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for opposing a move and the plural of the serving tops found in shops and pubs.

clue.text: Storms encountered on the way back annoying people

indicators.note: travelling back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: met means encountered
pests are annoying people

explanation.surface: A traveller meets bad weather and irritating folk on the return trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns MET into TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempests are violent storms.

clue.text: One gull picture

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to gull is to con or deceive

explanation.surface: A single seagull in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gull' looks like a seabird but is the verb to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a picture, especially a religious image painted on wood.

clue.text: Vague kind of article

definitions.meaning: in grammar 'a' and 'an' are the ... article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article is unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not precisely settled and also names the grammatical article a or an.

clue.text: Explanation needed for not being included in a race

indicators.note: one piece is included inside the other, placed within it

parts.note: a nation is a race or people
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks why they were left out of a running race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like a contest but is a people, a nation; 'being included in' puts NOT inside A NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An annotation is an explanatory note added to a text.

clue.text: Charge for Weill's opera?

parts.note: Kurt Weill wrote an opera named after a small old British coin, so the price of admission is jokingly that coin

explanation.walkthrough: Weill's The Threepenny Opera; threepence was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A threepence was an old British coin, so it could be the price charged, punning on Weill's opera title.

clue.text: Accumulation one's put back in the warehouse

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a depot is a warehouse

indicators.note: putting back means the letters are turned round

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone's goods pile up after being returned to the warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' gives I and S separately, which 'put back' turns round; 'Accumulation' means a built-up layer, not a stockpile in the warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a layer of material that has built up, such as silt or minerals.

clue.text: Like the common people, unequalled

definitions.meaning: commoners have no peerage, read as 'without peers', i.e. lords

explanation.surface: Ordinary folk are said to be beyond compare.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as without peers it describes commoners lacking a title, and normally it means having no equal.

clue.text: Game for a novel character

definitions.meaning: a bat-and-ball sport played in Britain and the Commonwealth
a talking insect appears in Dickens's The ... on the Hearth and in Pinocchio

explanation.surface: A sport is played for a character in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the British bat-and-ball sport and the insect that features as a character in Pinocchio and Dickens.

clue.text: Saw, for example, an angry wound

parts.note: cross means angry
a cut is a wound

explanation.surface: Someone's saw, say, has left a nasty gash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of 'see' but is the cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosscut saw is designed to cut across the grain of the wood, so a saw can be one.

clue.text: Dismissed team's in the field

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who is dismissed is out
a side is a team; the 's is linking

explanation.surface: A cricket team that is out takes the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side not batting is 'in the field'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out in the open air in a field is being outdoors.

clue.text: Little creature for use if model badly needed

indicators.note: done badly, the letters are jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: A small animal is needed if a model is poorly used.
explanation.definitionFit: A field mouse is a small wild rodent.

clue.text: "The years like great black tread the world" (Yeats)

definitions.text: "The years like great black tread the world" (Yeats)

parts.words: "The years like great black tread the world" (Yeats)
parts.note: a gap in a line of Yeats's poetry, to be filled with the beasts of burden he named

explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Yeats's play The Countess Cathleen; the blank is filled by the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeats compares the years to these large draught cattle trampling the world.

clue.text: Student loses his head on becoming the breadwinner

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a learner is a student

explanation.surface: A student drops out and becomes the family wage-earner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses his head' drops the first letter of LEARNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadwinner is the person whose wages support a household.

clue.text: Hay slung out for antelopes

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Hay is thrown out as feed for antelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: The nylghau, or nilgai, is a large Indian antelope.

clue.text: A measure of Israeli port

definitions.meaning: A port city in northern Israel

explanation.surface: Someone takes a measurement of a harbour in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a unit of land area and the historic port in northern Israel.

clue.text: One of Twain's travellers is not guilty

definitions.meaning: Twain's travel book is The ... Abroad

explanation.surface: A traveller in a Mark Twain book is acquitted.
explanation.definitionFit: It means blameless and also names one of the travellers in Twain's The Innocents Abroad.

clue.text: One tries to put one on the bed

definitions.meaning: a person who tests or samples
a canopy over a four-poster bed

explanation.surface: Someone tries to put another person on the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a person who tests things and the canopy above a four-poster bed.

clue.text: Simple, as Holmes said to Watson

definitions.meaning: the famous line attributed to Sherlock Holmes, '..., my dear Watson'

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes tells Dr Watson it is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: It means basic and easy and is the word in the line popularly given to Sherlock Holmes.
